Today Freya Axelsen had every chance of setting a new record. Right now three hundred and fifty thousand people were watching her stream, and that number was climbing fast as the broadcast moved into the Q&A segment.

If the live viewer count hit four hundred thousand, it would be an all-time world record for the entire coaching industry.

No one had ever pulled it off before her. Even the famous and obscenely rich Tony Bobbins, in his heyday, had only drawn three hundred and ninety thousand—and that was after decades in the market and with a face the whole world recognized! Now Freya had a shot at smashing through that ceiling with room to spare and securing her fame for years to come. And if anyone thought this was just dumb luck, Freya knew better: fortune favors only the prepared mind and the hands ready to act.

At first, things had gone merely okay. An hour went to a lecture on how to achieve your goals. It was the most enjoyable part, but only a hundred thousand showed up. Predictable, but not Freya's level—not with her four million on Instagram and another twelve on TikTok. Freya didn't like TikTok for its lack of a serious audience, but the algorithms had decided otherwise.

Another hour went to questions along the lines of "What's the best age to launch a startup?" and "How do I get up and start doing?" that followers had submitted through a form before the stream. The questions went over well and pushed the live count up to two hundred thousand.

But it still wasn't enough. It was a plateau. Two hundred thousand: a plateau that got harder to break through every time.

So Freya went all in, as the New York wheeler-dealers liked to say. In twenty minutes, right in the middle of the stream, her assistants bolted on a payment form and wrote up social media posts. And so began the surprise segment of the broadcast: open questions for donations. No moderation, but on Freya's terms.
